name: Active buzzer module (3-pin)
blurb: A buzzer board with its own oscillator: apply power to the signal pin and it beeps at a fixed pitch, no tone generation needed.

pins.name: VCC
pins.note: 3.3 to 5 V. The beep is louder at 5 V.

pins.name: I/O
pins.note: Most modules are low-level trigger: the buzzer sounds while this pin is LOW, so it beeps on power-up until the firmware sets the pin HIGH. The pin switches a transistor tied to VCC, so HIGH has to be close to VCC: from a 3.3 V controller, power the module from 3.3 V, not 5 V, or it never goes quiet. Check yours.

verify: Highly variable layout. With calipers measure: board length and width, buzzer diameter and height (12 x 9.5 mm assumed), header position and pin order as printed, and mounting hole presence (none assumed). Confirm trigger polarity (low-level or high-level) with a multimeter. Sound hole size is a design value for the enclosure, not a measured one.
sources: No datasheet opened. Commonly reported size of 3-pin low-level-trigger buzzer modules (about 32 x 13 mm, 12 mm buzzer).
